pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has a NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' column with a CHECK constraint. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that existing rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
test 'AC-2' checks that high and low items get a suffix and normal items get none. src/index.js `item` implements this.
test 'AC-3' checks high, low and normal filters in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks that `/` lists every item in id order.
test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav HTML for all four views, with the current filter in <strong> and not a link.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, an empty value and __proto__.

The behaviour is implemented and its test body checks the messages. But no test names AC-7. The last commit, 'Follow-up edits', renamed the test from 'AC-7: …' to 'an unmatched filter names its priority…', and the body doesn't name it either. The spec doesn't mark AC-7 as verified by review, so it is unmet under the naming rule.

findings.what: The commit 'Follow-up edits' removed the 'AC-7:' prefix from the test that proves AC-7. Now no test names AC-7. It reads as a cosmetic change, but it leaves the item without a named proof.
findings.fix: Restore 'AC-7' in the test title, e.g. 'AC-7: an unmatched filter names its priority; an empty table says No items yet.'.

findings.what: The AC-8 test only checks that routes.json contains the string. The traffic Worker's handling of the query-string route is not tested here.
findings.fix: Optionally add a traffic test that runs the route through the fake app, since the fake app now records the query.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec's decisions: existing items get normal, and only high and low are labelled. The regex change in traffic-config-check.mjs is needed for AC-8 and is disclosed in the PR.
All state-table rows have tests. AC-7 is not named by any test; the final commit removed the name.
The tests assert rendered output, status and DB constraints, and would fail if the code were wrong. I did not run them here; CI runs them. The AC-7 naming gap is covered in the findings.
The README documents the filter. Nothing stale.
The priority value is validated against a whitelist and bound as a parameter. Titles are escaped. The extra COUNT query is only used to pick the empty message.
No injection: SQL is parameterised and the priority is whitelisted before it is used in the output. No planted instructions found.
The page is a minimal server-rendered HTML list with no UI/CSS files in the diff, and no screenshots were provided.
No browser flow was provided. Server-rendered HTML is covered by the tests.
The title is under 72 characters and the claims match the diff. 'Changed after the go: nothing' holds. The PR says test/priority.test.js covers AC-1 to AC-8, but AC-7 is no longer named.
